features.feature_value: Kept posts to preserve opposing viewpoints visibility; prioritized free speech unless threats
features.evidence_span: I was thinking about free speech... If I decided to delete most of the posts, that means that the opposing viewpoints... wouldn’t have any visibility
features.rationale: The participant explicitly describes a decision rule balancing deletion against preserving viewpoint visibility under a free-speech principle.

features.feature_value: Removed content deemed hate-filled; framed focus as opinions vs hate speech
features.evidence_span: If something was hate filled I thought it should be removed.
features.rationale: They state a clear threshold for removal based on whether the content is hate-filled rather than merely an opinion.

features.feature_value: Compared original vs mirror by looking for attacks on the commenter vs opinion/continuing thought; removed attacks
features.evidence_span: looked for places they were attacking the commenter vs providing an opinion... The attacks I removed
features.rationale: Their strategy is specifically to distinguish attacking language from opinion when evaluating the pair.

features.feature_value: Used appropriateness of language (avoid cursing/personal attacks) as the main criterion
features.evidence_span: if they used appropriate language instead resorting to cursing or personal attacks.
features.rationale: They describe evaluating for cursing/personal attacks as the driver of influence.

features.feature_value: Used an 'elimination of the terms' style evaluation strategy
features.evidence_span: simple strategy of evaluation and elimination of the terms.
features.rationale: They characterize their method as a straightforward terms-elimination approach for deciding.

features.feature_value: Considered whether posts denied actual facts and whether they represented genuine beliefs
features.evidence_span: Whether they denied actual facts and whether they seemed to be genuine beliefs.
features.rationale: They list explicit evaluation dimensions about factual denial and authenticity.

features.feature_value: Noted many comments were rude and felt they should try to give better comments
features.evidence_span: many comments were rude... we should try and give better comments
features.rationale: The participant’s reasoning is grounded in perceived rudeness and a normative reaction to improve comment quality.
